title: How many types of writs are mentioned in the Constitution of India?
description: The Constitution empowers higher courts to issue specific writs for protection of legal and fundamental rights.
hint: The number is five.
summary: The five constitutional writs are Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo Warranto.

title: Which writ literally means 'produce the body'?
description: This writ is primarily used to secure the release of a person from unlawful detention.
hint: Its Latin meaning refers to producing the body.
summary: Habeas Corpus literally means 'you may have the body' and is used against unlawful detention.

title: Which writ is primarily used to secure release from unlawful detention?
description: The writ protects personal liberty by requiring justification for detention.
hint: Think of the writ associated with unlawful custody.
summary: Habeas Corpus is primarily used to challenge unlawful detention and secure release where the detention is illegal.

title: Which writ commands a public authority to perform a legal duty?
description: This writ is issued when a public authority or body fails to perform a duty imposed by law.
hint: Its name means 'we command'.
summary: Mandamus commands a public authority to perform a public or legal duty that it has failed to perform.

title: Which writ means 'we command'?
description: The terminology of Indian writ jurisdiction is largely derived from Latin legal terminology.
hint: It directs performance of a public duty.
summary: Mandamus is derived from Latin and means 'we command'.

title: Which writ prevents a lower court or tribunal from exceeding its jurisdiction?
description: This writ is preventive in nature and stops proceedings from continuing when the authority lacks jurisdiction.
hint: It operates before the lower authority completes the proceedings.
summary: Prohibition is issued by a higher court to prevent a lower court or tribunal from exceeding or exercising jurisdiction unlawfully.

title: Which writ is generally preventive rather than corrective?
description: One writ is used to prevent a lower judicial or quasi-judicial body from proceeding without jurisdiction.
hint: It stops proceedings before final decision.
summary: Prohibition is generally preventive because it restrains a lower court or tribunal from proceeding beyond its jurisdiction.

title: Which writ is generally issued to quash an order of a lower court or tribunal?
description: This writ has a corrective character and may invalidate a decision made without jurisdiction or with a serious legal error.
hint: It is often contrasted with Prohibition.
summary: Certiorari is used by a superior court to quash an order or decision of a lower court, tribunal or quasi-judicial body in appropriate cases.

title: Which writ literally means 'to be certified' or 'to be informed'?
description: The writ is associated with the supervisory jurisdiction of higher courts over lower judicial and quasi-judicial bodies.
hint: It can be used to quash certain decisions.
summary: Certiorari derives from Latin and is associated with the idea of being informed or certified.

title: Which writ challenges the legal authority of a person holding a public office?
description: The writ examines whether a person is legally entitled to occupy a public office.
hint: Its name asks 'by what authority?'.
summary: Quo Warranto challenges the authority by which a person holds a public office.

title: Which writ means 'by what authority'?
description: This writ questions the legal authority under which a person occupies a public office.
hint: The answer is a Latin legal term.
summary: Quo Warranto literally means 'by what authority'.

title: Which Article empowers the Supreme Court to issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
description: The Constitution gives the Supreme Court a specific writ jurisdiction for enforcing Fundamental Rights.
hint: It is Article 32.
summary: Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court to issue appropriate writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

title: Which Article empowers High Courts to issue writs?
description: High Courts have a broad constitutional writ jurisdiction under a specific article.
hint: It comes immediately after Article 225 in the Constitution.
summary: Article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for other purposes.

title: Which court has wider writ jurisdiction under the Constitution?
description: The Supreme Court and High Courts both possess writ jurisdiction, but their constitutional scopes differ.
hint: Consider Article 226.
summary: High Courts have wider writ jurisdiction because Article 226 permits writs for Fundamental Rights as well as for other purposes.

title: Under Article 32, writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court is primarily concerned with which purpose?
description: Article 32 is itself recognized as a Fundamental Right.
hint: Think about enforcement of Part III.
summary: Article 32 primarily provides a constitutional remedy for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

title: Under Article 226, High Courts can issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for what additional purpose?
description: The jurisdiction of High Courts under Article 226 is broader than that of the Supreme Court under Article 32.
hint: The phrase is 'for any other purpose'.
summary: High Courts can issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for other legal purposes under Article 226.

title: Which writ is most directly associated with protection of personal liberty?
description: The writ requires the detaining authority to justify the legality of detention.
hint: It is frequently described as a safeguard against unlawful detention.
summary: Habeas Corpus is a major constitutional remedy for protecting personal liberty against unlawful detention.

title: Against whom can a writ of Mandamus generally be issued?
description: Mandamus is directed toward performance of a public or legal duty.
hint: It is generally directed against a public authority or official.
summary: Mandamus may be issued against a public authority, public official, corporation or other body performing a public duty in appropriate circumstances.

options.title: A public authority failing to perform a legal duty
Only private individuals in every case

title: Which writ cannot generally be issued against a private individual for a purely private duty?
description: Mandamus requires a public or legal duty that is enforceable through this remedy.
hint: Think about public duty.
summary: Mandamus generally cannot be issued to enforce a purely private obligation against a private individual.

title: Which writ is issued to prevent a lower court from continuing proceedings beyond its jurisdiction?
description: The writ operates while proceedings are still pending before the lower authority.
hint: It is different from Certiorari, which is generally corrective.
summary: Prohibition prevents a lower court or tribunal from continuing proceedings beyond its jurisdiction.

title: Which writ is generally used after a lower court or tribunal has already passed an order?
description: This writ has a corrective function and may be used to quash an unlawful order.
hint: Compare it with the preventive writ Prohibition.
summary: Certiorari generally operates after a decision or order has been made by a lower court or tribunal and may quash it in appropriate circumstances.

title: Which writ can be used to challenge a person occupying a public office without satisfying the legal qualifications?
description: The writ protects the legality of public appointments.
hint: It asks the holder to show the authority for occupying the office.
summary: Quo Warranto may be issued when a person is unlawfully occupying a public office.

title: Which writ is generally not issued against the President or Governor for exercise of their official powers?
description: The Constitution provides specific protections concerning certain high constitutional offices.
hint: Consider Article 361.
summary: Mandamus is generally unavailable against the President or Governor for exercise of their constitutional powers because of the protections under Article 361.

title: Which writ is associated with the legality of detention rather than the legality of a public office?
description: Different writs address different constitutional and administrative wrongs.
hint: It protects personal liberty.
summary: Habeas Corpus addresses unlawful detention and protects personal liberty.

title: Which writ is most closely associated with checking whether a public office is legally held?
description: The writ tests the authority of a person to occupy a public office.
hint: Its name asks about authority.
summary: Quo Warranto is used to question the legal authority of a person holding a public office.

title: Which writ can be issued against a person illegally holding a public office?
description: The writ is concerned with usurpation of public office.
hint: It questions the authority of the office holder.
summary: Quo Warranto is the writ used to challenge unlawful occupation of a public office.

title: Which writ is generally directed against a judicial or quasi-judicial authority rather than a person illegally detained?
description: The writ is concerned with jurisdictional errors committed by lower adjudicating bodies.
hint: It can quash a decision.
summary: Certiorari is generally directed against judicial or quasi-judicial bodies to correct jurisdictional errors or certain legal defects.

title: Which writ is mainly concerned with stopping proceedings rather than quashing an already completed decision?
description: The distinction between Prohibition and Certiorari is important in constitutional law.
hint: It is preventive in nature.
summary: Prohibition primarily prevents a lower court or tribunal from proceeding beyond its jurisdiction.

title: Which writ can be sought by a person other than the detained person on behalf of the detainee?
description: The remedy is designed to protect personal liberty and does not necessarily require the detainee to approach the court personally.
hint: Think about unlawful detention.
summary: A petition for Habeas Corpus can be brought by a person acting on behalf of someone who is allegedly unlawfully detained.

title: Which writ is particularly important for enforcing a public authority's statutory duty?
description: The writ requires an authority to perform a duty imposed by law.
hint: It means 'we command'.
summary: Mandamus is an important remedy for compelling performance of a public or legal duty.

title: Which writ is known as a remedy against unlawful detention?
description: The writ requires the detaining authority to establish lawful grounds for custody.
hint: It is one of the oldest liberty-protecting writs.
summary: Habeas Corpus is a constitutional remedy against unlawful detention.

title: Which writ is generally not available to compel performance of a purely discretionary function?
description: Mandamus ordinarily requires an enforceable legal or public duty rather than a purely discretionary choice.
hint: The answer is the writ that commands performance of a duty.
summary: Mandamus generally cannot be used to compel an authority to exercise discretion in a particular manner where the law leaves the matter discretionary.

title: Which writ is associated with the phrase 'stop proceedings'?
description: This writ restrains a lower court or tribunal from continuing proceedings outside its jurisdiction.
hint: It is preventive.
summary: Prohibition is the writ used to stop a lower court or tribunal from proceeding beyond its jurisdiction.

title: Which writ is associated with quashing an order of an inferior judicial body?
description: The writ is corrective and examines certain jurisdictional or legal defects in the lower body's decision.
hint: It is commonly contrasted with Prohibition.
summary: Certiorari may be issued to quash an order or decision of an inferior court or tribunal in appropriate circumstances.

title: Which writ questions the authority of a person to hold a public office?
description: The writ protects the legality of public appointments and prevents unlawful occupation of public offices.
hint: It asks 'by what authority?'.
summary: Quo Warranto questions the legal authority of a person occupying a public office.

title: Which constitutional writ can be issued even when the detained person does not personally approach the court?
description: The remedy can be invoked by another person on behalf of someone whose liberty is allegedly unlawfully restricted.
hint: It concerns detention.
summary: Habeas Corpus can be sought by another person on behalf of the detained individual.

title: Which writ is concerned with a public office rather than a public duty?
description: One writ specifically examines whether an individual is legally entitled to occupy a public office.
hint: It concerns the authority of the office holder.
summary: Quo Warranto concerns unlawful occupation of a public office, whereas Mandamus concerns performance of a public duty.

title: Which writ is primarily used to compel an authority to perform a duty that it is legally bound to perform?
description: The writ is an important instrument of judicial control over public authorities.
hint: Its Latin name means 'we command'.
summary: Mandamus compels performance of a public or legal duty.

title: Which writ is associated with correction of jurisdictional errors by a lower tribunal?
description: A superior court can use this writ to review and quash certain decisions of inferior adjudicating bodies.
hint: It is corrective rather than preventive.
summary: Certiorari is used to correct certain jurisdictional errors and other recognized legal defects in decisions of lower judicial or quasi-judicial bodies.

title: Which writ prevents an inferior court from assuming jurisdiction that it does not possess?
description: The writ acts before the inferior authority completes the unlawful proceedings.
hint: It is a preventive writ.
summary: Prohibition prevents an inferior court or tribunal from proceeding in a matter beyond its jurisdiction.

title: Which writ can be used to challenge an unlawful detention by a private person?
description: Habeas Corpus is not restricted only to detention by government officials.
hint: The writ protects personal liberty regardless of who unlawfully detains the person.
summary: Habeas Corpus may be issued against unlawful detention even when the detention is by a private individual, subject to the facts and law.

title: Which writ is generally unavailable against a private individual when there is no public duty involved?
description: The writ requires a public or legal duty that the respondent is bound to perform.
hint: It commands performance of public duties.
summary: Mandamus generally cannot be issued to enforce a purely private obligation against a private individual.

title: Which writ can be issued against an authority exercising judicial or quasi-judicial functions?
description: Higher courts exercise supervisory constitutional jurisdiction over lower adjudicating bodies through specific writs.
hint: One such writ can quash an order.
summary: Certiorari may be issued against judicial or quasi-judicial authorities to correct recognized jurisdictional or legal errors.

title: Which writ is preventive in relation to the jurisdiction of an inferior court?
description: The writ stops an inferior authority from proceeding beyond its lawful jurisdiction.
hint: Its name is also an English word meaning a restriction or ban.
summary: Prohibition is the preventive writ used to restrain an inferior court or tribunal from exceeding jurisdiction.

title: Which writ is concerned with the legality of occupying a public office?
description: The writ is intended to prevent a person from unlawfully holding a public office.
hint: It asks the office holder to establish authority.
summary: Quo Warranto examines whether a person has lawful authority to occupy a public office.

title: Which Article makes the right to constitutional remedies a Fundamental Right?
description: The Constitution guarantees access to the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
hint: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar described it as one of the most important provisions of the Constitution.
summary: Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

title: Which court can issue writs for purposes beyond enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
description: The Constitution gives High Courts broader writ jurisdiction than the Supreme Court under Article 32.
hint: Look at Article 226.
summary: High Courts can issue writs under Article 226 for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for other purposes.

title: Which writ is generally considered the most direct constitutional remedy against illegal detention?
description: It requires the authority responsible for detention to produce the detained person before the court.
hint: Its Latin name refers to the body.
summary: Habeas Corpus is the principal writ remedy against unlawful detention.

title: Which writ is primarily used to compel performance of a public duty rather than review a judicial decision?
description: The writ is an important remedy against failure by a public authority to perform a legal obligation.
hint: It means 'we command'.
summary: Mandamus is used to compel performance of a public or legal duty.

title: Which pair of writs is most closely associated with controlling the jurisdiction of lower courts?
description: Two writs are particularly important in supervising inferior courts and tribunals.
hint: One prevents proceedings and the other can quash a decision.
summary: Prohibition prevents an inferior court or tribunal from exceeding jurisdiction, while Certiorari can quash an unlawful decision in appropriate circumstances.
